title: Choose Tagalong's visual world
question: The roll assigned Pocket Pet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pocket Pet
options.thesis: Every pet lives in its own little LCD window; the app is the candy-coloured shell around them.
options.viewport: Crew Office: crew rail left, the office as one recessed LCD scene with pets at desks and rooms, meetings panel right.
options.risk: Reads as a toy to technical users if the LCD spreads from the pets into the controls.

raised.raise: Pet state is an LCD icon plus a word, never colour alone.
One UI face with a strict five-step scale; pixel type only on pet names and LCD readouts.
A meeting reads as a time column whose length is its model calls.
A meeting's call cap is a visible meter that fills, like a tape that must not overflow.

options.label: Party Menu
options.thesis: Your crew is an adventuring party: one job class each, abilities equipped, a top-down office map.
options.viewport: Party list with job classes on the left, the office as a 16-bit map, meeting log in a bordered window.
options.risk: The blue RPG window is the most familiar retro move there is; it reads as pastiche if overused.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: The crew as a cast of mascots, each with a name plate, a role and a one-line note.
options.viewport: A roster grid of pets with name plates and role notes; the office opens from a pet's cell.
options.case: Fuses well: the directory card becomes a name plate. Wins clarity on crew screens, loses identity on the office.
options.risk: Can tip into kawaii merchandise and away from a working tool.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.lineage: printed zoo and garden guide maps
options.thesis: The office as a guide map: desks and meeting rooms are flat colour lobes, pets stand on the coastlines.
options.viewport: The office floor as a map of lobes, each room a colour, with capsule labels for live meetings.
options.case: Rooms read instantly as places; flat vector fights the pinned pixel-art feel.
options.risk: Loses the pixel game feel the brand asked for.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: State as hatch density on stacked translucent sheets.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets over a zone wedge.
options.case: Neither audience recognises a darkroom record.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Registration marks and hairlines on near-white stock.
options.viewport: A plate grid with one grotesque.
options.case: Too austere for warm and playful.
options.risk: Reads as a portfolio, not a crew.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Time runs up a centre staff; length is duration.
options.viewport: A vertical staff of meeting turns.
options.case: Nobody in either audience reads a dance score.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Two sides, timed to fit the tape exactly.
options.case: Charming, but says music, not a working crew.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern desktop tool, with pixel pets only as avatars.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, office canvas and meetings panel, executed like the best productivity apps.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other AI assistants by design.
